rationale: Re-request the execution for the Node-wrapper question on the corrected harness. The pump now honours the application's persistence duty, and the verified draft run shows a conforming prefix (node 2 applies the bootstrap entry, the removal and the re-add in order) together with the same witness: Propose succeeds before the removal (0ms, leader log index 2) and is blocked after the re-add (301ms, context deadline exceeded, leader log index unchanged at 4) while node 2 is a member again and still knows leader 1 in term 1. The diagnostic campaign block was removed because it hung the harness after the witness, so the restore path stays outside this basis; the comparison set now uses only fields the events carry at the top level.

scope.description: Observe the application-facing proposal path of the Node wrapper for one wrapped node 2 that leader 1 removes from the configuration and then adds back in the same term, with the application duties of the Ready/Advance contract honoured (entries, hard state and snapshots persisted before messages are sent), comparing Propose before the removal and after the re-add together with the leader's log index around each call.
assumptions: Two voters {1,2} in one process: node 2 is driven through the Node wrapper (newNodeTestHarness, Readys consumed, entries/hard state persisted, Advance called) while node 1 is a bare raft instance driven by the harness's message pump; node 1 is made leader directly and broadcasts its appends.

Both nodes apply the removal and the re-add through the application path (n1.applyConfChange and the wrapper's ApplyConfChange), and every snapshot of node 2 is taken through its status channel (node.Status), executed inside the run loop.
Propose is called with a 300ms context deadline.
excluded: The leadership-change restore path: the diagnostic attempt was removed from the harness because it hung after the witness, so it is not part of this basis.

experiment.prefix: Create the wrapped node 2 over its own storage and a bare node 1 over storages with voters {1,2}; make node 1 leader at term 1 and broadcast its appends; pump messages (persisting whatever node 2's Readys carry) until node 2 knows leader 1 and has applied the bootstrap entry; propose through the wrapper and record the outcome; propose the removal of node 2 on node 1, pump, and apply it on both nodes; propose the re-add of node 2 on node 1, pump, and apply it on both nodes; then propose through the wrapper again and record the outcome and the leader's log index around it.
experiment.requirement: Node.Propose is the application-facing proposal path: its documentation states that it proposes data to be appended to the log and warns only that proposals can be lost without notice (node.go:138-140). A node that the application has added back to the configuration, and that knows the leader of that configuration, must therefore be able to hand a proposal to raft - or report why it cannot - rather than block until the caller's context expires while the group never sees the proposal.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the wrapper's own bookkeeping decides whether the application's proposals reach the group, and the target's comment at node.go:409-411 records that this bookkeeping is unsound.

comparisons.description: Control: while node 2 is a plain member of {1,2} and knows leader 1, Propose returns no error.
Control: the proposal forwarded by the follower reaches the group - the leader's log index is 2 after the call (the bootstrap entry plus this proposal).
Premise on the witness event: the leader's configuration contains node 2 again after the re-add.
Premise on the witness event: the wrapped node still knows leader 1, in the same term, so the leadership is unchanged across the removal and the re-add.
Witness: with node 2 a member again and still knowing leader 1, Propose returns only when its context deadline fires (context deadline exceeded after about 300ms).
Witness: the proposal never reached the group - the leader's log index is unchanged at 4 across the call.

experiment.revision_reason: The pump now performs the application's persistence duty (Ready.Entries written to the wrapped node's storage, Ready.Snapshot applied, non-empty Ready.HardState persisted, all before the Ready's messages are sent and before Advance) so the basis is a prefix a conforming application produces; the diagnostic campaign block that hung the harness after the witness was removed and the comparison set is reduced to the observations whose fields the events carry at the top level. The witness is unchanged in substance.
